prompt: The word hydraulics comes from the Greek word for:
options: Force
Water
Pressure
Motion
explanation: Water.

prompt: How is a pressure change transmitted in a confined fluid at rest?
options: Equally throughout the fluid, but reduced at the container walls
Only in the direction of the applied force
With a pressure loss proportional to the container width
Equally and undiminished throughout the fluid and to its container walls
explanation: The pressure change is transmitted equally and undiminished throughout the fluid and to the container walls.

prompt: Four open containers hold the same liquid to the same vertical depth. Their shapes and volumes differ. How does the pressure at the bottom compare?
options: The largest volume produces the highest pressure.
The widest container produces the highest pressure.
All four have the same bottom pressure.
The narrowest container produces the highest pressure.
explanation: All four have the same bottom pressure. For the same liquid, pressure depends on vertical depth rather than container shape or volume.

prompt: Which arrangement increases output force in an ideal hydraulic system?
options: Use an output piston with a larger area than the input piston
Use an output piston with a smaller area than the input piston
Use equal input and output piston areas
Increase output travel while keeping input and output piston areas equal
explanation: Larger output piston area. It produces greater force at the same pressure, with less output travel for a given input stroke.

prompt: Which property is a liquid’s internal resistance to flow?
options: Viscosity
Density
Compressibility
Chemical stability
explanation: Viscosity.

prompt: A liquid flows slowly under the same conditions as a faster-flowing liquid. Which description generally fits the slower liquid?
options: Higher viscosity
Lower viscosity
Lower flash point
Higher chemical stability
explanation: Higher viscosity.

prompt: What generally happens to hydraulic-liquid viscosity as temperature decreases?
options: It increases
It decreases
It remains constant
It changes only if fluid volume changes
explanation: It increases.

prompt: Two different hydraulic fluids are at 30°F. What can be concluded about their viscosity?
options: Equal temperature does not guarantee equal viscosity
Their viscosities must be equal
The larger fluid volume must have higher viscosity
Their viscosities depend only on container shape
explanation: Equal temperature does not guarantee equal viscosity.

prompt: Which distinction between viscosity and pressure is correct?
options: Viscosity is resistance to flow; pressure is force per unit area
Viscosity is force per unit area; pressure is resistance to flow
Viscosity measures density; pressure measures the amount of stored fluid
Viscosity and pressure describe the same fluid property
explanation: Viscosity is resistance to flow; pressure is force per unit area.

prompt: Which instrument is used to measure viscosity in the supplied slides?
options: Saybolt universal viscosimeter
Bourdon pressure gauge
Hydrometer for density
Thermometer for flash-point testing
explanation: Saybolt universal viscosimeter.

prompt: Which pairing correctly distinguishes flash point, fire point, and chemical stability?
options: Flash: sustained burning; fire: momentary ignition; stability: resistance to deterioration
Flash: momentary ignition; fire: resistance to deterioration; stability: sustained burning
Flash: resistance to deterioration; fire: sustained burning; stability: momentary ignition
Flash: momentary ignition; fire: sustained burning; stability: resistance to deterioration
explanation: Flash: momentary ignition; fire: sustained burning; stability: resistance to deterioration.

prompt: Which colour-to-fluid mapping matches the samples and specifications in this presentation?
options: Vegetable: red; mineral MIL-H-5606: blue; phosphate ester: light purple
Vegetable: blue; mineral MIL-H-5606: light purple; phosphate ester: red
Vegetable MIL-H-7644: blue; mineral MIL-H-5606: red; phosphate ester: light purple
Vegetable: light purple; mineral MIL-H-5606: red; phosphate ester: blue
explanation: Vegetable MIL-H-7644: blue; mineral MIL-H-5606: red; phosphate ester: light purple.

prompt: Which base-fluid and brand pairing is correct?
options: Vegetable: petroleum; mineral: castor oil/alcohol; phosphate ester: Skydrol
Vegetable: castor oil/alcohol; mineral: Skydrol; phosphate ester: petroleum
Vegetable: castor oil/alcohol; mineral: petroleum; phosphate ester: Skydrol
Vegetable: Skydrol; mineral: petroleum; phosphate ester: castor oil/alcohol
explanation: Vegetable: castor oil/alcohol; mineral: petroleum; phosphate ester: Skydrol.

prompt: Which seal-material mapping matches the three fluid families in the slides?
options: Vegetable: neoprene; mineral: natural rubber; phosphate ester: butyl or ethylene-propylene
Vegetable: natural rubber; mineral: butyl; phosphate ester: neoprene
Vegetable: natural rubber; mineral: neoprene; phosphate ester: butyl or ethylene-propylene
Vegetable: butyl; mineral: neoprene; phosphate ester: natural rubber
explanation: Vegetable: natural rubber; mineral: neoprene; phosphate ester: butyl or ethylene-propylene.

prompt: Which statement correctly associates the listed fluid characteristics?
options: MIL-H-7644 is mineral-base; MIL-H-5606 is phosphate ester; vegetable fluid is the listed fire-resistant fluid
MIL-H-7644 is phosphate ester; MIL-H-5606 is vegetable-base; mineral fluid is Skydrol
MIL-H-7644 is vegetable-base; MIL-H-5606 uses anti-foam/corrosion additives; phosphate ester is fire-resistant
MIL-H-7644 is vegetable-base; MIL-H-5606 is Skydrol; phosphate ester uses natural-rubber seals
explanation: MIL-H-7644 is vegetable-base; MIL-H-5606 uses anti-foam/corrosion additives; phosphate ester is fire-resistant.

prompt: MIL-H-83282 is backward compatible with which listed fluid specification?
options: MIL-H-7644
MIL-H-5606
BMS 3-11
A phosphate-ester Skydrol specification

prompt: Which fluid-and-seal pairing is unsuitable according to the presentation?
options: Phosphate ester with butyl rubber
Phosphate ester with ethylene-propylene elastomer
Phosphate ester with neoprene
Mineral MIL-H-5606 with neoprene
explanation: Neoprene is unsuitable for phosphate ester such as Skydrol; it is listed for mineral MIL-H-5606 instead.

prompt: Which set contains only desirable hydraulic-fluid characteristics?
options: Low flow resistance, chemical stability, lubrication, and seal compatibility
Low flow resistance, easy compression, lubrication, and seal compatibility
Chemical stability, corrosion protection, retained air bubbles, and seal compatibility
Chemical stability, lubrication, foaming tendency, and low flow resistance
explanation: Hydraulic fluid should lubricate, remain chemically stable, resist corrosion, and be compatible with the system. It should resist compression and avoid foaming or retaining air bubbles.

prompt: Why should hydraulic systems and fluid containers be kept sealed?
options: To prevent viscosity changes while allowing air to enter
To isolate pressure while allowing moisture to escape through open ports
To stop oxidation by replacing all reservoir air with hydraulic fluid
To exclude contamination, air, and moisture
explanation: Sealing helps exclude contamination, air and moisture. Incompatible fluids can swell or damage seals, cause seal breakdown and block the system. Slide 47 specifically identifies 83282 as backward compatible with 5606.

prompt: What is a possible consequence of mixing incompatible hydraulic fluids?
options: Improved seal flexibility without a compatibility check
Lower viscosity with no effect on seals
Improved fire resistance with unchanged seal compatibility
Seal swelling or breakdown and system blockage
explanation: Sealing helps exclude contamination, air and moisture. Incompatible fluids can swell or damage seals, cause seal breakdown and block the system. Slide 47 specifically identifies 83282 as backward compatible with 5606.

prompt: Which system allows fluid to circulate from the reservoir, through the pump and neutral selector valves, and back to the reservoir without maintaining stored operating pressure?
options: Closed-centre system.
Open-centre system.
A sealed accumulator alone.
A brake deboost system alone.
explanation: Open-centre system.

prompt: Which selector-valve arrangement matches the systems described in the slides?
options: Open centre: parallel; closed centre: series
Open centre: series; closed centre: parallel
Both systems: series
Both systems: parallel
explanation: Open centre: series; closed centre: parallel.

prompt: Which comparison of open- and closed-centre systems matches the presentation?
options: Closed centre is generally simpler; open centre stores energy with an accumulator and check valves
Open centre is generally simpler; closed centre can store energy with an accumulator and check valves
Both systems store operating energy through neutral return flow
Both systems depend on thermal relief valves for energy storage
explanation: Open centre is generally simpler; closed centre can store energy with an accumulator and check valves.

prompt: Which comparison of neutral flow and simultaneous operation is correct?
options: Closed centre circulates through neutral selectors; open centre supplies several components at once
Open centre circulates through neutral selectors; closed centre can supply several components at once
Open centre blocks all neutral flow; closed centre returns all pump flow through every selector
Both systems require all selectors in series for simultaneous operation
explanation: Open centre circulates through neutral selectors; closed centre can supply several components at once.

prompt: In a closed-centre system, which statement correctly describes actuator supply?
options: Pressure remains available; fluid flows to an actuator when it is commanded
Pressure disappears in neutral; fluid continuously flows through each actuator
Fluid continuously flows through neutral selectors while no pressure is stored
Pressure is created only by the reservoir when an actuator is commanded
explanation: Pressure remains available; fluid flows to an actuator when it is commanded.

prompt: Which arrangement can store hydraulic energy for later use?
options: Open centre with neutral selectors providing a continuous return path
Closed centre with an accumulator and check valves
Open centre with a regulator but no energy-storage component
Closed centre with a reservoir and no energy-storage component
explanation: Closed centre with an accumulator and check valves.

prompt: What is a hydraulic power pack?
options: A self-contained hydraulic power system
A reservoir-and-accumulator assembly without a pump
A pressure-control valve installed in the return line
An actuator assembly supplied by a separate central power system
explanation: A self-contained hydraulic power system.

prompt: Which set contains the four power-pack components listed in the presentation?
options: Electric pump, pressure-control valves, selector valves, reservoir
Electric pump, pressure-control valves, selector valves, accumulator instead of reservoir
Electric pump, pressure-control valves, actuator, reservoir instead of selector valves
Engine-driven pump, actuator, accumulator, reservoir
explanation: Electric pump, pressure-control valves, selector valves, reservoir.

prompt: Which reservoir identification matches the two diagrams?
options: Left: in-line, connected by tubing; right: integral, built into the power pack
Both are integral reservoirs built into their power packs
Both are in-line reservoirs separate from their power packs
Left: integral, built into the power pack; right: in-line, connected by tubing
explanation: Left: integral, built into the power pack; right: in-line, connected by tubing.

prompt: Which pair describes reservoir functions besides storing fluid?
options: Purging air and allowing thermal expansion
Regulating normal system pressure and lowering brake pressure
Storing pressurized energy and controlling actuator direction
Reducing actuator pressure and unloading pump flow
explanation: Any two: purging air, separating contamination, allowing thermal expansion, accommodating changes in system fluid-volume requirements.

prompt: Why is a pressurized reservoir useful at high altitude?
options: It increases actuator force by replacing the system pressure regulator
It removes contamination by forcing it through the accumulator
It eliminates the need to allow for thermal expansion
It maintains positive pump-inlet supply and helps prevent foaming
explanation: Provides a positive fluid supply at the pump inlet and helps prevent foaming. Methods: aspirator, bleed air and hydraulic system pressure/bootstrap.

prompt: Which three reservoir-pressurizing methods are listed in the slides?
options: Aspirator, ambient ram air alone, and thermal relief
Bleed air, pressure reducer, and actuator return spring
Bootstrap, accumulator discharge alone, and reservoir filter
Aspirator, bleed air, and hydraulic system pressure/bootstrap
explanation: Provides a positive fluid supply at the pump inlet and helps prevent foaming. Methods: aspirator, bleed air and hydraulic system pressure/bootstrap.

prompt: The early brake system using a rubber expander tube is described as:
options: An open-centre hydraulic system
A closed hydraulic system
A continuous-circulation hydraulic system
A pneumatic brake system
explanation: Closed hydraulic system.

prompt: Which brake type does the presentation identify as the modern aircraft arrangement?
options: Expander-tube brakes
Floating disc brakes
Drum brakes
Band brakes
explanation: Floating disc brakes.

prompt: Which actuator comparison is correct?
options: Single-acting: fluid on one side with spring/nitrogen opposition; double-acting: fluid on both sides
Single-acting: fluid on both sides; double-acting: fluid on one side with spring/nitrogen opposition
Both use fluid on one side, but only double-acting uses a return spring
Both use fluid on both sides, but only single-acting uses a selector valve
explanation: Single-acting: fluid on one side with spring/nitrogen opposition; double-acting: fluid on both sides.

prompt: Which function belongs to the pressure regulator?
options: Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit
Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating
Maintains lower pressure for a component
Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range
explanation: Pressure regulator: Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range.

prompt: Which function belongs to the system pressure relief valve?
options: Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range
Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating
Maintains lower pressure for a component
Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit
explanation: System pressure relief valve: Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit.

prompt: Which function belongs to the thermal relief valve?
options: Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range
Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit
Maintains lower pressure for a component
Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating
explanation: Thermal relief valve: Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating.

prompt: Which function belongs to the pressure reducer?
options: Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range
Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit
Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating
Maintains lower pressure for a component
explanation: Pressure reducer: Maintains lower pressure for a component.

prompt: Which function belongs to the debooster?
options: Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range
Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit
Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating
Reduces pressure while increasing fluid volume delivered to brake actuators
explanation: Debooster: Reduces pressure while increasing fluid volume delivered to brake actuators.

prompt: Which function belongs to the unloading valve?
options: Controls normal system pressure within a preset operating range
Protects against pressure exceeding the normal operating limit
Protects isolated fluid from pressure caused by heating
Returns excess pump flow when required pressure is reached
explanation: Unloading valve: Returns excess pump flow when required pressure is reached.

prompt: If the regulator fails and pressure rises excessively, which component provides overpressure protection?
options: Thermal relief valve
Pressure reducer
System pressure relief valve
Debooster
explanation: System pressure relief valve.

Reservoir
Filter

prompt: Which system and selector arrangement are shown in the diagram?
options: Closed centre with selectors in parallel
Open centre with selectors in parallel
Open centre with selectors in series
Closed centre with selectors in series
explanation: Open centre with selectors in series.

prompt: With the illustrated selectors neutral, which flow path applies?
options: Reservoir → pump → accumulator, with neutral selector flow blocked
Pump → actuators on both sides, with no reservoir return
Reservoir → pump → neutral selectors → reservoir
Reservoir → selectors → pump, bypassing the neutral return path
explanation: Reservoir → pump → neutral selectors → reservoir.

prompt: Which fluid identification matches this comparison, including the BMS 3-11 sample?
options: Left red: phosphate ester/BMS 3-11; right purple: mineral MIL-H-5606
Left red: mineral MIL-H-5606; right purple: phosphate ester/BMS 3-11
Left red: vegetable MIL-H-7644; right purple: phosphate ester/BMS 3-11
Left red: mineral MIL-H-5606; right purple: vegetable MIL-H-7644
explanation: In this comparison the red sample represents mineral MIL-H-5606, and the purple sample represents phosphate ester such as Skydrol/HyJet (BMS 3-11). Colour alone cannot identify every specification; MIL-H-83282 is also red.

prompt: Which formula represents hydraulic pressure? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: P = F / A
P = F × A
P = A / F
P = F × D
explanation: P = F / A.

prompt: Which formula represents hydraulic force? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: F = P × A
F = P / A
F = A / P
F = P × D
explanation: F = P × A.

prompt: Which formula represents piston area from force and pressure? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: A = F / P
A = F × P
A = P / F
A = F / D
explanation: A = F / P.

prompt: Which formula represents circular piston area from radius? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: A = π × r²
A = 2 × π × r
A = π × r
A = π × diameter²
explanation: A = π × r².

prompt: Which formula represents displaced fluid volume? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: V = A × D
V = A / D
V = D / A
V = F × D
explanation: V = A × D.

prompt: Which formula represents work? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: W = F × D
W = F / D
W = F × D / t
W = P × A
explanation: W = F × D.

prompt: Which formula represents power? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: Power = F × D / t
Power = F × D × t
Power = F × D
Power = F / (D × t)
explanation: Power = F × D / t.

prompt: Which formula represents horsepower using feet and minutes? F = force, A = area, D = distance, P = pressure, r = radius, and t = time.
options: hp = F × D / t
